Quick technical notes for the sim run (to avoid rework):

- Cache modeling: assume prefix cache hit is applied at request level before generation. For Helix we should run hit rates of 15%, 30%, 50% (20%/50% from Sarah is fine; adding 30% midline helps interpolation). Prefetch overhead = +5% token write (metadata) — include in costs.
- Effective tokens per request = prompt_tokens + completion_tokens - (prefix_saved_tokens * hit_rate).
- Batching: measuring tokens/$ alone is insufficient — report both tokens/$ and tokens/sec (throughput) and p95 latency for each batch size. For small prompts batching=32 may push p95 above 800ms depending on model; simulate p95 under both constant and burst traffic.
- Quantization: we will simulate int8-ish using our quant profile 'q8_fast' and fp16 baseline. Note quality delta is small for NLU tasks but might degrade long completion coherence — include a short quality-estimate note.
- Warm KV-cache effects: include a warmup curve (0–48 hours) and show steady-state vs cold-start tokens.

I’ll run sims on a 100k/150k/250k DAU profile matrix and attach the raw CSV by EOD tomorrow. Ben — please run the batching latencies on your rig and add p50/p95/p99.

-Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
